results.title: Engineer Cadet - Higher National Diploma Programme | Warsash Maritime
excerpts:
This fully-sponsored cadet training programme leads to a HND Marine Engineering, as well as the award of a UK Maritime and Coastguard Agency (MCA) Certificate of Competency (STCW’95 III/I OOW).
What you'll study
Phase 1
* 27 weeks
* Maritime Electrical Machines
* Maritime Mathematics for Engineers
* Maritime Thermodynamics and Mechanics
* MNTB Workshop Skills and Technology
* STCW Basic Safety Training Week
Phase 2
* 28 weeks
Phase 3
* 32 weeks
* Operational Electrical and Electronic Control Systems
* Operational Marine Engineering Knowledge
* Operational Maritime Law and Project Management
* Operational Naval Architecture and Stability (Engineering)
* MNTB Workshop Skills; IAMI EK and MCA oral examination preparation
* 34 weeks
* Law and Business for Marine Engineers
* Maritime Applied Mechanics
* Maritime Applied Thermodynamics
* Maritime Electrical and Electronic Control Systems
* Marine Electro-Technology
* Naval Architecture and Ship Construction
* Shipboard Management
* Completion of MNTB Workshop Skills
To apply for an HND in marine engineering, you must undertake a three year engineer officer cadet training programme approved by the Merchant Navy Training Board (MNTB) and meet the academic entry requirements as stated.
The next step is to find a company to sponsor you so that you can complete the sea service elements of the training programme.

Management Level (III/2) Engineering Knowledge (EK) Examination Syllabus
Published 3 November 2017
Contents
Candidates should have knowledge of current and emerging technologies, practises and operation techniques required for the operation and maintenance of machinery, equipment and ship structure usually in charge of the Chief Engineering officer.
Candidates are required to understand the legal and management responsibilities of the rank of Chief Engineer officer.
Candidates should be well acquainted with machinery and boiler causalities which may occur at sea and be able to state how these can be prevented or remedied.
The candidate to have knowledge of the following:
